item.text:
**4B.7 Research Note**
Kishida’s 2024 record is mostly pro-equality on the dimensions that were actually visible in the sources: anti-discrimination rhetoric, women’s empowerment, redress for forced sterilization victims, democracy language, and support for local regions. The main negatives are structural and policy-level rather than direct repression: Japan still has persistent inequality for women, minorities, LGBT+ people, and noncitizens, and Kishida’s “illegal foreigners zero” line signals tighter exclusionary migration control.

- [Video Message by Prime Minister Kishida at the Symposium on Inclusive Society and Human Rights](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202402/05_message.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | February 5, 2024 | Kishida explicitly rejected discriminatory treatment against foreigners, people with disabilities, the Ainu, and sexual minorities, and said the government would stand firm against prejudice. This is direct positive evidence for protecting political equality for excluded groups. | Question IDs: 4B.7

- [Video Message from Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio on International Women’s Day](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202403/08message2.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | March 8, 2024 | Kishida tied women’s empowerment to gender equality, wage parity, executive appointments, support for work-family balance, and anti-sexual-violence measures. This is strong affirmative evidence for women’s political and social equality. | Question IDs: 4B.7

- [Video Message from Prime Minister Kishida to the 29th International Conference for Women in Business](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202407/29message.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | July 29, 2024 | Kishida set a 30 percent female board-member target for listed firms and emphasized female leadership, entrepreneurship, and work compatibility. This supports a reading that he actively tried to widen women’s access to decision-making. | Question IDs: 4B.7

- [Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida Regarding the Ruling on a Lawsuit over the Former Eugenics Protection Law and Other Matters](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202407/03kaiken.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | July 3, 2024 | Kishida apologized for forced sterilization under the former Eugenics Protection Law, called it a human-rights violation, and promised compensation and new guarantees. This is direct redress for a state abuse against a vulnerable group. | Question IDs: 4B.7

- [National Statement (Commitment) Video Message by Prime Minister Kishida on the Occasion of the Third Summit for Democracy](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202403/20message.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | March 20, 2024 | Kishida reaffirmed democracy, supported election observer missions abroad, and framed women’s and children’s rights as part of a human-dignity agenda. This is supportive evidence for equal political standing and for respecting contested viewpoints. | Question IDs: 4B.7

- [Policy Speech by Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio to the 213th Session of the Diet](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | January 30, 2024 | Kishida said local regions must be protected, repeated that regional vitalization is essential, and linked policy to local transport, tourism, and rural resilience. This is positive evidence for treating opposition or peripheral regions as worthy of equal public support rather than neglect. | Question IDs: 4B.7

- [Meeting of the Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202404/19keizai.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | April 19, 2024 | Kishida said local communities need sustainable administrative services and focused support for regional revitalization, including digital tools and grants. That is direct evidence of trying to avoid a center-only allocation of opportunity. | Question IDs: 4B.7

- [Press Conference by Prime Minster Kishida](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202406/21kaiken.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | June 21, 2024 | Kishida said expanded local-government subsidies would reduce burdens on low-income households and support school lunches, public transport, childcare, and regional services. This is evidence of redistribution toward weaker localities and lower-income groups. | Question IDs: 4B.7

- [岸田文雄のウソ？ホント？](https://kishida.gr.jp/fact/) | Kishida Fumio official website / LDP-affiliated site | 2024 page content | The page defends a tougher “illegal foreigners zero” agenda, including stricter residency revocations, advance entry screening, and tighter refugee procedures. This is the clearest mixed/negative signal: it is administrative exclusionary control over migrants, though I found no evidence of direct political intimidation or collective punishment. | Question IDs: 4B.7

- [Japan: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/japan/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | Freedom House says Japan is free, but it flags outstanding ethnic and gender discrimination, underrepresentation of women, exclusion of some ethnic Koreans from elections because of citizenship rules, and weak equality for LGBT+ people and asylum seekers. This is negative structural evidence that Kishida did not eliminate inequality, even if the sources do not show him personally engineering it in 2024. | Question IDs: 4B.7

**Search gap**
I did not find reliable 2024 evidence that Kishida directly suppressed opposition regions, punished unpopular viewpoints, or imposed explicit unequal political rights through state coercion. The strongest negative material is structural and preexisting in Japan’s institutions, plus the more restrictive migration posture on the LDP-affiliated Kishida site.
